title: A smooth compactly supported autocorrelation potential with ground-state nondegeneracy on a nonempty interval of masses
difficulty_reason: After reusing old2153 fixed-mass H1/frequency convergence and taking Newton nondegeneracy/coercivity and the Riesz self-convolution identity as named inputs, one H2 construction remains. A directly truncated or mollified Newton kernel need not be a self-convolution of a smooth nonnegative radial compactly supported decreasing form function. The authors build that constrained autocorrelation family, control both its local L3/2 and far-field uniform limit, and track two independent scales so that fixing their product leaves a nonempty interval of masses for the same fixed potential and every positive radial minimizer. Fixed-mass perturbative coercivity alone cannot supply this interval. The supporting spectral transfer and scaling identities belong to this single unit; neither a second H2 nor a new H3 is counted.

editorial_notes: Keep particle dimension d distinct from environment dimension n>=3. H2 form functions are nonnegative smooth compactly supported and radial; H3 adds nonincreasing sigma1.

Admissibility Definition2.6 quantifies over a mass interval of nonempty interior and every positive radial minimizer, with coercivity constants allowed to depend on mass/potential/ground state. No general uniqueness inferred.

Old2153 is Proposition2.13(i) only: original literal locator2.13-i, statement835-851/proof1743-1859 and original specific H3 judgment remain. Secondary selects common header+item(i)835-842; full context is not wider adoption.

New Proposition2.11/8.2 construction in d3: distinguish preliminary directly truncated potential2051-2053 from actual autocorrelation construction2088-2112. Normalize integral alpha=1/sqrt(C), take epsilon=lambda*mu fixed and m in(mu0^-1*M,lambda0*epsilon^-1*M). The same fixed potential serves the interval; no claim of uniform coercivity constant over it.

New support includes Proposition2.13(ii) proof1861-1919 and Lemma7.1, rather than treating them as already adopted through old wide context. Lenzmann/Newton spectral kernel and DAvenia-Squassina coercivity and the Riesz convolution identity are named inputs, not recounted units.

Theorem2.2 concerns the full set of ground states. Theorem2.8 concerns the chosen phase/translation orbit conditionally on admissibility and equal mass; c-weighted wave-velocity norm, c-uniform eta/delta and the equal-mass restriction are preserved.

The speculative d2 subsection does not remove d2 from the earlier general-d existence/set-stability theorems. Its Questions1-3 and Conjecture1.2 remain open; exponential stopping is not established by orbital stability.

AppendixA: mixed time/space norm matching under smooth convolution, Banach contraction and mass/energy continuation; no separate H2. AppendixB: Lions-Paul Wigner/Husimi compactness, weak wave equicontinuity, compact translated smooth-kernel force tests and kinetic-tail estimate; the added smooth-wave transfer is below separate H2. AppendixC is dimensional context.
